follow_caller.description: Answer each caller in whichever selected language they speak. Accepted at creation so a multilingual agent can be created in one request; enabling it requires at least two languages and is refused with 400 otherwise. Creation stores the opt-in only -- the first PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}/voice-stack publication is what proves one shared transcriber can listen for the selected set, and refuses the publication when none can. Changing it afterwards is a voice-stack save, not an agent update. An engine without a language axis (see voice_frontend) REFUSES this field with 400 rather than accepting and dropping it.

language_profiles.description: When supplied this replaces the sparse override set; omit it to preserve overrides. Each item has locale and optional exact voice, transcriber, and greeting. Omitted values inherit the shared stack; an empty greeting removes its override.

languages.description: The languages this agent may answer in. An engine without a language axis (see voice_frontend and the agent-catalog conversation_engines block) REFUSES this field with 400 rather than accepting and dropping it.

oneOf.description: Exact selected TTS provider/model/voice inventory item.

voice_id.description: Provider inventory id, when the selected provider exposes voices.

AgentAcknowledgements.description: Optional short acknowledgement while a slow reply is still being prepared: at most one per caller turn, spoken in the agent's own voice, model and current language on a separate outgoing track, cancelled the moment the real reply starts. Off unless enabled. Without phrases the platform's reviewed list for the call language is used; a language without one stays silent rather than switching to English.

delay_ms.description: How long the reply may take before an acknowledgement is worth speaking.

phrases.description: Bounded neutral phrases; digits and currency marks are rejected so a phrase cannot carry a factual, payment, legal or consent claim.

AgentAnswerDetection.description: What the platform does when a call the carrier reported answered turns out not to be a person: non-human audio such as a caller tune, or a voicemail box. Unlike the other tuning sections, a value you send here is STORED even when it equals the current default, and only an ABSENT `answer_detection` key means "follow the platform default". That is deliberate: the platform default for this setting is expected to change once the detector has been measured, and an agent that explicitly chose a value keeps it when that happens. Applied when a call starts; saving never changes an in-progress call.

non_human_audio.description: `shadow` records what was heard on every answered call and changes nothing the caller experiences: the classification and its detail appear on the call, and no call is ever ended by it. `end_call` acts on the verdict: the agent stops speaking and the call is ended with `ended_reason: no_human_after_answer`, and the classification and its detail appear on the call as they do under `shadow`. `off` collects nothing, so such a call carries no classification at all. `shadow` is the platform default, so it is what an agent with no stored value gets; sending it explicitly stores it, which is how you keep it if that default later moves. This property carries no JSON Schema `default` on purpose, unlike the other tuning properties: a generated client that pre-filled one would send `shadow` on every save and pin a choice the customer never made, which is the one outcome the storage rule above exists to prevent.

voicemail.description: What the AI agent does when a voicemail box answers an outbound call. Voicemail is judged from the first seconds of audio after the answer; the phone network does not report it. Only mailbox-specific evidence counts as proof: a record beep that follows a spoken greeting, or a mailbox instruction such as "leave a message", from a language whose phrase list is verified (en; English is checked on every call). The beep works in every language. The greeting before it must reach three recognised words, counted by the spaces and punctuation between them, so in Chinese, Japanese, Thai and other scripts written without spaces a short greeting is undercounted, and a beep after it only raises suspicion. Candidate phrase lists (de, es, et, fr, ru) are not yet verified: what they recognise is shown as evidence and never proves a mailbox. In any other language only the beep or an English instruction can. A fast answer, a long greeting or music only raise suspicion, and a call the platform is unsure about is treated as a person. `shadow` (watch only) records the verdict and what the platform would have done on the call in Calls, and changes nothing the caller experiences. `hang_up` ends the call without a message on proof of a mailbox. `leave_message` plays the `voicemail_messages` entry for the call's language after the beep, once per contact, and hangs up without a message when there is none for that language. `off` detects nothing. `hang_up` and `leave_message` are accepted and stored now but currently run as `shadow`: they start acting only after the detector has passed its accuracy check, and each call's evidence shows both the chosen and the effective mode. `shadow` is the platform default; like `non_human_audio`, an explicitly sent value is stored even when it equals the default, and this property carries no JSON Schema `default`. The `answer_detection` object is replaced as a whole on save, so send every key you want to keep.

voicemail_messages.description: The messages left when `voicemail` is `leave_message`, one per language, keyed by language code (`{"en": "...", "et": "..."}`); a locale such as `de-DE` is stored as `de`. `leave_message` requires at least one. The message played is the one for the language the call is actually in; a call in a language with no message is ended without one, never given a message in another language. Plain text; runs of whitespace are collapsed, a blank text removes that language's message, and control characters are refused. Each message is played exactly as approved, never improvised by the AI agent, so keep it neutral: who is calling and how to call back, with no account, amount or other personal details, because a voicemail box can be heard by someone other than the person you meant to reach. Messages are kept when `voicemail` changes to another mode and for languages the agent no longer offers.

events.description: Subscribed event types. Omitted or empty at creation defaults to call.created, call.answered, media.started, call.ended, call.completed, call.failed, call.canceled. Change it later with PATCH /v1/agent-endpoints/{agent_endpoint_id}.
The complete replacement subscription list; an empty array is rejected.

AgentFollowCaller.description: Explicit saved and published automatic multilingual policy. Existing clients may send only enabled; omitted scope means selected. With scope all, the server resolves every language compatible with the exact stack at publication and freezes that concrete set. With selected, languages supplies the allowed subset. Clients cannot supply runtime adapter options, bindings, or rates.

scope.description: Valid only when enabled. Omit for selected compatibility. All is expanded only at explicit publication and can be unavailable when a provider candidate limit is smaller than the compatible set.

AgentLanguageProfiles.description: Safe editor projection. The immutable runtime profile and credential binding IDs are never returned. Published Follow summaries expose only the frozen allowed locale set, opt-in bit, and opening locale for the authenticated test picker.

published_at.description: ISO 8601 publication time. An empty string with published_version 0 is the legacy-agent sentinel: no language-profile publication exists yet.

published_languages.description: Locales from the immutable published profile set. This is empty when no publication exists.

published_starting_language.description: Frozen Follow opening locale for the published browser-test picker, or an empty string when Follow is not enabled.

AgentModelUnresponsive.description: How long the agent may stay silent after the caller has finished speaking before the platform ends the call. It exists because a conversation engine can stop answering without saying so: a provider outage mid-call leaves the line up, the caller talking to nobody and the call billing, and on some engines nothing at all is reported. It counts only time the line was free: the clock starts when a caller turn ends, it does NOT run while the caller is speaking (their own speech is subtracted, so a caller who keeps talking is never cut off mid-sentence, and one who pauses between attempts still reaches the bound), and it is cleared the moment the agent produces anything — a reply, a tool call, or the end of the call. It also never runs while the agent is speaking, while a tool is running, before the caller's first turn, or on a call whose replies come from a workflow. A call ended this way reports `ended_reason` `agent_unresponsive` with `reason_detail` `model_unresponsive` (calls completed before 2026-09-25 reported `model_session_lost` with the same detail). On by default at the platform's own bound; an absent section is that default and is not stored.

seconds.description: The bound, in seconds. `0` switches it off, and is the only value outside the range: an agent that waits on something genuinely slow may need it. Otherwise 10 to 120. The platform's own bound applies when unset.

AgentTool.description: A legacy string placeholder, a built-in tool, a signed webhook tool, or an attached Integration Action.

AgentToolWait.description: What the caller hears while a slow tool call (an integration action, a knowledge search) is still running. Off unless a mode is set. `sound` plays a quiet keyboard-typing bed on the separate outgoing track once the tool has run for `delay_ms`, cut the instant the tool finishes, capped at 15 seconds; it is wordless, so it works in every language. `acknowledge` speaks one short phrase in the agent's own voice and language instead; without phrases the platform's reviewed list for the call language is used, and a language without one stays silent. Feedback never plays over the caller or the agent, at most once per tool wait, and never for the built-in end-call or transfer tools.

delay_ms.description: How long a tool may run before feedback starts. Most tools finish well inside this.

phrases.description: For `acknowledge` only; the same bounded neutral-phrase rule as acknowledgements. Rejected with `sound`.

AgentTurnTaking.description: Per-agent barge-in and endpointing tuning. Every field is optional and omitted from responses when it is at its default, so an agent that has never configured this section has no `turn_taking` key at all. Applied when a call starts; saving never changes an in-progress call.

barge_in_speech_rms.description: Deprecated. Accepted, stored and returned for compatibility only; this runtime does not apply it to call behavior. Use `interruption_sensitivity`, `min_speech_ms` and `min_interruption_words` to control interruptions.

interruption_sensitivity.description: Hosted phone calls in every language. Preset interruption threshold: balanced 500 ms (the default), low 750 ms, high 150 ms. Preset end-of-turn hold on a language with the trained turn detector: balanced 200 ms (the default), low 520 ms, high 260 ms; on a language without one, where the hold is the whole end-of-turn decision: balanced 800 ms (the default), low 1100 ms, high 600 ms. An explicit `min_speech_ms` or `silence_hold_ms` takes precedence over the preset for its knob.

max_call_seconds.description: How long a call may run before the platform ends it and reports `ended_reason: max_call_duration_reached`. Defaults to 1740 (29 minutes), which is also the ceiling: the underlying media session is dropped at 30 minutes, and a limit above that could never fire, so the call would end with no reason attached. Lower it to cap a call sooner; a value outside the range is refused rather than clamped.

min_interruption_words.description: Defaults to 1 on hosted ENGLISH phone calls and to 0 everywhere else; set 0 explicitly to disable it. When set, an interruption must ALSO carry at least this many recognized words from the caller, in addition to the speech-duration threshold; it never lowers that threshold. On hosted ENGLISH calls, short listening noises ("mm-hm", "uh-huh", "yeah", "okay", "right", "sure", and filler words such as "uh") do not count toward it, so a caller showing they are following does not interrupt; every word counts in other languages. Not English-only, but effective only on stacks whose transcriber reports words fast enough to land inside the decision window (today the Deepgram stacks, English and Estonian). Elsewhere it is stored, returned unchanged, and ignored at call time.

min_speech_ms.description: Hosted phone calls in every language. Explicit continuous-speech threshold before an interruption is considered; it overrides any sensitivity preset. On a phone call the value is honoured down to 150 ms; a value below 150 ms is raised to 150 ms. A phone call with no value set and no sensitivity preset uses the 500 ms default. Browser and web calls do not apply this value at all: it is still stored and returned, but those calls keep the stack's own threshold.

no_caller_speech_seconds.description: How long after the call is answered the platform waits to hear the other party before ending the call and reporting `ended_reason: no_caller_speech_after_answer`. Defaults to 20. Speech is detected from the audio itself, not from a transcript, and once the other party has been heard once the rule does not apply again for the rest of that call. The floor is 10 because the witness is voice activity: a caller who is merely listening looks the same as one who is not there, and a shorter value ends the call partway through the agent's own opening line.

silence_hold_ms.description: Hosted phone calls in every language. Explicit endpointing delay after the caller stops speaking; it overrides the platform default hold and any sensitivity preset.

AgentUnrecognisedSpeech.description: What the agent does when the caller speaks and the transcriber produces nothing at all — most often a caller using a language the agent's transcriber is not listening for, but also a bad line or a dropout. The agent says one short line in the call's own language telling the caller it could not understand them and which languages it can help in, then keeps listening; it never guesses what was said, never calls a tool and never ends the call. It is spoken only after the caller has stopped talking and the platform's wait for a transcript has expired, so it cannot talk over a live caller, and it is skipped entirely on an agent with follow-the-caller enabled, where the language switch answers instead. On by default, and spoken at most twice per call unless you change `max_per_call`. Send `enabled: false` to switch it off; an absent section is the default and is not stored.

enabled.description: `false` switches the line off for this agent, and is the only value stored: the behaviour is on for every agent that says nothing.

max_per_call.description: How many times one call may hear it. Two when unset.

phrase.description: Your own wording, spoken verbatim in place of the line the agent would otherwise compose in the call's language. Write it in the agent's language: it is not translated.

AgentUpdate.description: Mutable agent configuration. The target agent, rather than organization_id or project_id in this body, defines the authenticated workspace boundary. Voice-stack settings are not part of this payload: turn_taking, voice_polish, answer_detection, audio_environment, follow_caller, languages and language_profiles are saved by PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}/voice-stack, and sending one here is refused with 400 naming that route rather than accepted and dropped.

status.description: Whether this agent is offered to callers. `inactive` stops it being admitted on every call path -- inbound and outbound telephony, the browser test, and the public homepage demo -- while keeping the agent, its configuration and its number attachments intact; a call already in progress is not torn down. `active` removes that gate and nothing else: no configuration is snapshotted or restored, so the agent is then admitted on its CURRENT published configuration and readiness, which may have changed while it was inactive. Accepts these two values only; any other is refused with 400, as is any change to an agent whose stored status is not already one of them (an operator-suspended agent is reinstated by an operator only).

tools.description: Complete agent tool allowlist. To attach an Integration Action, use an AgentTool object whose type is connection.

oneOf.description: Exact selected TTS provider/model/voice inventory item.

voice_id.description: Provider inventory id, when the selected provider exposes voices.

AgentVoicePolish.description: Per-agent voice polish. Absent keys keep the platform defaults; the response omits the section entirely when nothing is configured.

delivery.description: How the selected voice performs its speech. Unset keeps the provider's own defaults, which is what every agent had before this field existed. Each profile maps to allowlisted provider controls only where the selected TTS provider/model truthfully exposes them: ElevenLabs voice settings (eleven_v3 supports stability only), a bounded Gemini TTS synthesis instruction, and a speaking-rate multiplier for Soniox and Cartesia. Fish Audio and Azure neural voices accept the setting but apply no change. The voice preview (POST /v1/voice-previews with the same `delivery`) uses the identical mapping, so an audition sounds like the call.

AgentVoiceStack.description: Safe read projection. It never includes component credential binding IDs, plaintext/ciphertext, nonce, fingerprint, or provider secrets.

voice.description: The stored TTS selection as the agent catalog projects it, including `delivery_control` (`voice_settings`, `instruction`, `speed` or `unsupported`): whether a `voice_polish.delivery` profile changes this voice's audio, and `delivery_profiles`: the exact value each profile resolves to on this engine (empty for `unsupported`), both read from the packaged delivery table.

voice_frontend.description: The conversation engine; cascade is the default. Always present on GET; omitted on older rows means cascade. Whether this engine has a language axis is declared in the agent-catalog conversation_engines block (has_language_axis).

AgentVoiceStackUpdate.description: Selection/update payload. It carries only selectors, existing credential IDs, tools, and tuning -- never provider secret material. Supplying languages replaces the selected set; supplying language_profiles replaces sparse overrides, while omission preserves them. After language opt-in, shared prompt, stack, or credential saves explicitly republish inherited effective profiles.

component_credential_bindings.description: Optional stt/llm/tts map to existing hosted-AI credential IDs (or null to use platform-managed selection). References are validated; secret upload is a separate write-only API.

language_profile_revision.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency revision returned by GET. A stale value returns conflict; reload before retrying.

language_profiles.description: When supplied this replaces the sparse override set; omit it to preserve overrides. An engine without a language axis (see voice_frontend and the agent-catalog conversation_engines block) REFUSES this field with 400 rather than accepting and dropping it.

languages.description: When supplied this replaces the selected language set. An engine without a language axis (see voice_frontend and the agent-catalog conversation_engines block) REFUSES this field with 400 rather than accepting and dropping it.

voice_frontend.description: Optional conversation engine. Omitted or cascade is STT/LLM/TTS. gpt_live selects GPT-Live-1. GET still returns transcriber, model, and voice as an OpenAI compatibility projection. Each engine declares whether it has a language axis; a voice-to-voice engine does not, and this route then refuses languages, language_profiles and follow_caller with a 400 naming the field and the engine. Read has_language_axis from the agent-catalog conversation_engines block rather than assuming it from the id.

workflow.description: Editable draft/revision, validation, and safe canvas-only layout when workflow_state=draft; otherwise null.

layout.description: Only positions, viewport, and collapsed_groups; arbitrary stored layout keys are not returned.

AudioEnvironmentInvalidSelection.description: A historic malformed saved pin, returned visibly instead of silently becoming Off. Choose a supported selection or Off before publishing again.

asset_version.description: Immutable packaged asset version; it is never inferred.

preset_id.description: Exact catalogue id. `off` has no asset.

volume.description: Whole-number selection. Off requires 0; enabled presets require 1 through 100.

BuiltinAgentTool.description: A built-in tool the AI agent can invoke during a call. `phone_number` is conditionally required: see its own description.

phone_number.description: Destination for `transfer_to_human`, and required when that tool is enabled. Must be full E.164 including the leading `+` and country code (for example `+12025550100`); a blank, partial, or non-dialable number is rejected when the agent is created or updated, rather than failing mid-call. Ignored by `end_call` and `send_sms`.

ref.description: Read-only, server-issued. A stable opaque identifier for this configured tool, used to name the tool on a call's transcript rows without storing the tool's own name with them. Ignored if you send it: the value is taken from what is already stored, so it cannot be chosen. It survives any edit that keeps the tool's `name` and `type`; renaming, retyping or removing a tool retires its identifier, and transcript rows recorded before that show the tool's kind instead of a name.

Call.description: The call resource GET /v1/calls and GET /v1/calls/{call_id} return. A synthetic simulation or platform-internal room is never returned here; only a call the customer or their agent actually made.

answer_classification.description: What was heard after the call was answered, which is a different question from whether it was answered at all: a carrier bridges audio for a ringback replacement tune or a hold-music loop exactly as it does for a person, so the status says the line answered and this says what was on it. `human` means a person was heard. `non_human_audio` means nothing a person did was ever heard: continuous music or tones held the line, or a recording repeated the same cycle of things over and over; `reason_detail` names which kind. `silent` means the line answered and nothing at all was heard. `unknown` means the detector ran and reached no decision inside its window, which is deliberately NOT the same as the empty string: empty means no verdict was reported at all, on a call placed before this field shipped, on an agent whose collection is switched off, or on a call whose media never started. Detection is deliberately narrow and only claims `non_human_audio` for unbroken non-human audio, so a recorded announcement or an IVR menu with pauses in it reads as `human` or `unknown` rather than being classified here -- unless it repeats itself, which is the one text-based verdict, `looping_recording`.

call_context.description: The small, non-secret JSON object you supplied at call creation.

direction.description: inbound, outbound, or web_test (a live browser test) for a call your agent placed or answered. A call seeded by the demo/artifact-import tooling can carry other values, such as imported, verbatim from that import.

ended_reason.description: Why the call ended. They fall into three groups. Two are the ordinary end of a call that went well: `agent_completed` when the agent finished the conversation and ended the call itself, which is the usual outcome of a workflow that runs to its last step, and `remote_party_disconnected` when the other party hung up. Six are endings the platform initiates: `agent_unresponsive`, described below, `hangup_requested` when someone ends the call from the workspace or through POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/hangup, `max_call_duration_reached` when the call hits its configured limit, `no_caller_speech_after_answer` when the call is answered but nobody ever speaks, `no_human_after_answer` when the call is answered but nothing on the line was a person: only music or tones were ever heard, or a recording repeated the same cycle of things over and over, and `caller_unresponsive` when both sides fell silent after the agent had spoken: after 30 seconds of silence the agent asks whether the caller is still there (once per silent stretch, at most three times per call), and the call ends politely 15 seconds after that question if nobody answers. This ending is rolling out: while it is in observation the platform records what it would have done and does not end calls, so the value does not yet appear. A caller who answers, even with one word, simply continues the conversation. The last two name an ending nobody chose, neither the people on the call nor the platform: `media_session_lost`, when the media session went away underneath a live call -- the room was deleted, or the connection to it failed -- and `model_session_lost`, when the conversation engine behind the call failed and could not be recovered while the media session was still up, so the platform ended the call rather than leave the line open with nobody on it. `agent_unresponsive` is the platform ending a call whose agent stopped answering while its engine stayed connected: the caller finished speaking and the agent produced nothing for the whole of the agent's `voice_polish.model_unresponsive` bound, which counts only the time the caller was NOT speaking. It reports `reason_detail` `model_unresponsive`. It says what was observed -- a silent agent -- and not that anything failed, because a voice-to-voice engine reports nothing when it stops answering. Calls completed before 2026-09-25 reported this ending as `model_session_lost` with the same `reason_detail`. In all three, nobody hung up, no limit fired and the agent did not finish. Each reports what was observed rather than guessing at a cause, so a call that ends this way is not reported as an operator hang-up even when an operator had just asked for one; that request is answered separately and says the call was already gone. Empty on a call that completed before this field shipped, and on a call that has not completed. A call that FAILED reports its reason in `technical_failure.failure_reason_code` instead; the two vocabularies are separate.

estimated_cost_minor.description: The wallet reservation estimate in minor currency units, made at admission time. This is not settled billing: some statuses hold no reservation at all (see NO_LEDGER_MOVEMENT statuses), and a completed call's real charge is settled separately from recording/artifact import.

external_reference.description: Your own stable case/reference ID, echoed back verbatim; empty string when not set. The same value delivered in webhook event bodies.

from_number_id.description: Your owned number this call used, when applicable.

provider_call_id.description: The carrier/provider's own call identifier. Empty until the call is actually dialed out to the provider.

purpose.description: Required, free-form outbound purpose declaration -- a non-empty purpose is the compliance paper trail; a novel purpose token is never refused for being novel. Documented catalog (pick one or send your own token): appointment, booking_confirmation, callback_requested, customer_outreach, delivery_notification, ops_alert, other, payment_reminder, personal_errand, reservation, status_check, support.

reason_detail.description: Qualifies either `answer_classification` or `ended_reason`, and says which by the value. `caller_tune`, `hold_music` and `looping_recording` appear only with `answer_classification` `non_human_audio`, and `no_audio` only with `silent`: `looping_recording` means the far end said the same cycle of things over and over, a recording on repeat, rather than music or tones. `model_unresponsive` appears with `ended_reason` `agent_unresponsive` -- and, on calls completed before 2026-09-25, with `model_session_lost` -- and means the call was ended by the platform because the agent produced nothing at all for the whole of its bound of caller-free time after the caller finished speaking -- as opposed to the same reason reached because the conversation engine reported its own failure. Empty when neither needs qualifying, which is most calls. This is not `ended_reason` itself: that one names the ending, this one adds to it.

recipient_type.description: Optional, never enforced or required -- outbound is not restricted to business recipients. Persisted verbatim on the call row if sent; SMS has no recipient_type column, so it is accepted but not stored there.

recording.description: Present only once a recording exists for this call.

transcript_status.description: partial means a transcript exists but is missing the text of at least one spoken agent reply.

recording_status.description: not_started or disabled when there is no recording yet, otherwise the latest recording's own status.

runtime_config.description: Your own per-call overrides captured at call start (e.g. instructions, first_message, language). Never provider credentials.

source_kind.description: Always 'live' on this customer-facing route -- a simulation-suite or other synthetic room is not found here at all.

status.description: Call lifecycle status, e.g. requested, queued, dialing, ringing, answered, in_progress, media_started, completed, failed, busy, no_answer, canceled, live_blocked, policy_blocked, needs_review. Not a closed set: track it as an opaque string and rely on the call.* events for exact transitions.

CallEvent.description: One row of a call's internal lifecycle log, oldest first. Not the webhook envelope: this row's own id/type/payload, never the signed delivery body. Includes many types never delivered to any webhook endpoint at all.

page_cursor.description: This row's position in the timeline. Pass the LAST row's value as `after` to continue from here. Opaque: its encoding is not part of the contract, and it is not the row's id.

payload.description: Event-specific detail; shape varies by writer, not just by type -- call.failed alone has at least four shapes: a policy block carries {reason, reasons}; local/queued-origination failure carries {reason} (the worker-queue originate failure adds worker_job_id and error); a reconciler repair carries {source, reason, previous_status, evidence, observed_at}; a gateway-lifecycle failure (SIP/room) carries an unrelated {gateway_event_id, gateway_id, source_component, source, observed_at, details}. Always thinner than the richer result body the call.failed webhook delivers separately.

type.description: e.g. call.created, call.queued, call.dialing, call.answered, media.started, call.ended, call.failed, call.canceled, call.live_blocked, plus internal-only bookkeeping types such as wallet.reserved, wallet.settled, call.authorization, call.policy_evaluated, number.matched. call.completed is the one terminal type never written here -- it is only ever delivered to webhooks.

answered_or_voicemail.description: Observed call.answered/media.started evidence: the transport answered. It is not a human answer classification and can be voicemail, a caller tune or hold music. Read `call.answer_classification` for what was actually heard on the line.

summary.description: Factual counters only. answered_or_voicemail publishes numerator and denominator; human_answered/voicemail remain unavailable unless independently observable. Per-call answer classification is published on each item rather than summarised here, because a summary counter would imply a coverage this summary cannot promise for calls placed before the classification existed.

CallRecording.description: Metadata for the active recording. Use download_url for playback; storage_key and media_url are legacy implementation details, not download contracts.

download_url.description: Relative authenticated API URL for full or byte-range recording playback.

CallRecordingState.description: Safe recording-disclosure state (services/calls_routing/calls.py:_call_recording_state_from_rows). recording_state and recording_disclosure on Call both carry this same object.

active_recording_id.description: Empty string unless the latest recording is undeleted and available.

media_url.description: Empty string unless a recording is currently active.

recording_id.description: Empty string when there is no recording yet.

status.description: not_started or disabled when there is no recording yet, otherwise the latest recording's own status (e.g. processing, available, deleted).

CallResultCallReference.description: Authoritative technical call facts, intentionally separate from advisory extraction.

answer_classification.description: What was heard after the answer, with the same meanings as on the Call resource. It sits here rather than with the analysis because it is an observation of the line, not a reading of the conversation.

reason_detail.description: Qualifies answer_classification or ended_reason, with the same meanings as on the Call resource.

agent_window.description: Present only when you requested one.

agents.description: Present only when agent_window was requested: one bounded page of agents that have placed or received a call in this scope, ordered by agent_id. Read agents_has_more before treating it as the whole set.

agents_has_more.description: Present only when agent_window was requested. True when the organization has more agents than this page holds; the page is NOT the whole set unless this is false.

agents_limit.description: Present only when agent_window was requested: the page size actually applied, after clamping.

agents_next_cursor.description: Present only when agent_window was requested. Non-empty only when agents_has_more is true: pass it as agent_after to continue. Empty string on the last page.

agents_returned.description: Present only when agent_window was requested: agents in this page.

project_id.description: Empty string when the request was not scoped to one project.

windows.description: Keyed by the window key you supplied in the repeated window=<key>:<since> query parameter.

calls.description: Calls for this agent within agent_window.

last_call_at.description: Most recent call for this agent across the whole history, not just agent_window.

spend_minor.description: Same estimated_cost_minor sum as CallStatsWindow.spend_minor, scoped to this agent within agent_window.

answered.description: Calls in this window somebody was on: completed, or currently answered/in_progress/media_started. Never merely accepted by the platform.

get.description: Pass metered_only=true to receive only the launch-supported hosted components with a runtime adapter, native meter, pinned retail rate, and safe credential contract (validated BYOK where supported or an explicit platform-managed provider contract). The payload also includes conversation_engines: cascade (default STT/LLM/TTS) and gpt_live (GPT-Live-1 voices and Responses backends). Every engine row carries has_language_axis: true for cascade, false for a voice-to-voice engine that has no separate transcriber, LLM or TTS and therefore no language set, no per-language profile overrides and no Follow the caller. Read that flag rather than matching on the engine id: agent create and the voice-stack PATCH refuse languages / language_profiles / follow_caller for an engine whose row says false. A TTS row uses either immutable worker-approved voices or bounded provider-directory voices already ingested by Skysay; the catalog never fetches a provider during a read. Voice metadata and tags are provider-supplied and carry provenance; Skysay does not infer age, accent, or personality. When a provider supplies no per-voice language list, the row inherits only its qualified TTS model languages. voice_count and voices_truncated say when a provider inventory is partial. A resolved agent preserves its exact selected voice in its voice-stack response even outside a bounded catalog slice. Every TTS row carries `delivery_control`: `voice_settings`, `instruction` or `speed` when a `voice_polish.delivery` profile changes that engine's audio, or `unsupported` when the engine accepts and stores a profile without changing its audio (Fish Audio and Azure neural voices today); and `delivery_profiles`, the exact value each of the four profiles resolves to on that engine (a settings object such as stability/similarity_boost/style/speed, a speaking rate, or an instruction sentence), empty for `unsupported`. Both are read from the same packaged delivery table the call runtime and the voice preview use, so a client can state what a profile changes for a voice without a provider list of its own. Each tts entry also lists default_languages: the languages in `languages` where the voice may be chosen WITHOUT the owner choosing it (for example as the pre-selected voice of a new agent). A voice can run a language without being its default -- ElevenLabs eleven_v3 runs English but lists only Estonian -- and a client that pre-selects voices should respect it. This catalog does not authorize a provider credential or disclose provider secrets.

post.description: Workspace-authenticated only. Does not use the anonymous homepage demo budget. New sessions reserve eligible browser-only welcome credit or purchased funds and settle actual component usage; no carrier charge applies. The existing session limit is 180 seconds. Historical zero-charge snapshots remain unchanged. The selected snapshot is published or a validated draft overlay. A draft overlay naming an unknown, retired, or language-incompatible selection is rejected with a plain 400 before this point, as before. Beyond that, the resolved realtime configuration -- the agent's stack merged with any draft overlay -- is checked for runnability before anything is reserved; a config the voice worker would refuse before building media (missing prompt/first message, missing provider/model/voice, or an unsupported language) is refused here instead of reaching the worker.

A stack with no `voice_frontend` is a partial cascade overlay on the stored engine. A draft stack is refused while Follow the caller is published for the agent.

post.description: A text chat test of the agent as a browser voice test would run it, minus audio: the same resolved configuration (system prompt, opening line, language profile, tools, attached knowledge, and for snapshot=draft the editor's unsaved overlay), the same built-in tool prompt appends and the same language directive the voice worker applies, answered by the agent's configured Gemini model. Stateless: send the transcript so far and the new caller_input; caller_input=null with an empty transcript asks for the opening line (the configured first message verbatim, or one generated from the instructions when none is configured). Tool policy: search_knowledge_base runs the real retrieval; end_call ends the chat (ended=true, ended_reason=end_call); every other tool -- send_sms, transfer_to_human, webhook, connection and legacy MCP allowlist tools -- is HELD: the model is told the action did not happen and the call is reported in events with disposition=held. Nothing is persisted and no call record is created. Platform-funded: no wallet reservation and no component charge (only the model ran); metering reports the model calls and tokens this turn consumed. Bounded: 2000 characters per message, 40 transcript lines (the chat ends with ended_reason=transcript_limit), 24000 transcript characters, 4 tool rounds per turn and a 20-second turn budget. Refused with 400 for an agent that has a conversation flow, is not hosted, not active, GPT-Live, bound to a customer-owned model credential, or has no instructions; when no platform model credential is configured; or when the model does not answer in time. An agent WITH a conversation flow is refused with 400 here (a call with it runs the flow, so a prompt-only answer would be one no call gives) and is tested through the workflow run routes instead.

get.description: The automation surface: built for a CI job rather than for a screen. contract_version is the promise -- fields may be ADDED under the same version, but nothing is removed or given a new meaning without it changing, so a client can ignore what it does not recognise and keep working. Attempts paginate on a stable cursor with an explicit has_more; the query count does not grow with the number of attempts. Statuses are a closed set: a run is queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled or budget_exceeded, and an attempt is pass, fail or error. errored_cases is deliberately separate from failed_cases -- an attempt whose synthetic caller or evaluator malfunctioned produced no evidence about the agent, so treating it as a failure would fail a build for a platform outage. voice_evidence_kind says which voice proof an attempt carries: offline_robustness means the authored lines were synthesized and read back, and makes no claim about barge-in, overlapping audio, playout or SIP timing; only realtime evidence can support a timing claim. unproven_assertions counts rules the attempt could not settle for want of that evidence -- they are neither passes nor failures. Transcripts, recordings and rubric rationales are not included; artifacts reports whether each is still retained, expired, or never existed.

scenarios.description: Authored caller scenarios. At most 50 per suite. Each scenario's turns carry what the caller does and when: kind is speech, backchannel or silence; a silence turn carries silence_ms and no caller_input, because a silence is time rather than words; cue.after_agent_turn (1-based, and 0 meaning no cue at all: take the turn when the agent finishes) and cue.delay_ms record where inside an observed agent turn the caller speaks. Multiple cues anchored to the same turn share that observed origin, and an unobserved cue or incomplete schedule produces no scenario timing proof rather than an invented one. ground_truth_variants records alternative renderings of the same line -- a numeral written as digits or as words, say -- so a run's stored evidence carries what the caller was authored to say in every form that counts as correct. The platform's own offline recognition metric still scores against caller_input alone; the variants are carried for the readiness scorer that reads them. A silence turn needs the adaptive_voice runner and is refused with 422 silence_needs_a_room on any other, because only a room has time to spend. An adaptive_voice scenario may also carry caller_environment: a version-pinned synthetic caller MICROPHONE condition using noise_level (not the agent audio_environment volume). A scenario that supplies caller_environment must use adaptive_voice and also supply a non-blank language; it is never silently changed to English. Off/noise_level=0 is the quiet baseline; it never changes the agent's output ambience, TTS, or production STT configuration. A saved condition is authoring data, not proof that this deployment ran a realtime room.

post.description: Requests teardown of a call that is already live. This is also what the Hang up button on a live call in the workspace Calls page sends. Returns 202 with `hangup_requested_at`; it never reports the call as ended, because the media session is torn down by the worker holding it and the call reaches `call.ended` through the ordinary terminal path. The call then reports `ended_reason` `hangup_requested`, unless it had already started ending another way, in which case that ending's reason is reported. Repeating the request is idempotent and returns the original timestamp. Until a worker acknowledges, the request stays visible with `status` `pending`. If the worker reports that the teardown FAILED, the call is still up, so a further request re-arms it with a fresh timestamp and the previous failure's reason stays visible beside it; after three consecutive failed teardowns further requests are refused so the call is escalated rather than retried. A call still queued for origination is refused: cancel it with POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/cancel instead. For a workspace caller, a call in another workspace, or a Simulations Lab run, answers exactly as a call id that does not exist. The response carries `hangup_requested_at`, `status` (`pending` or `acknowledged`), `hangup_acknowledged_at`, `hangup_acknowledged_outcome`, `hangup_acknowledged_reason`, `hangup_failed_attempts`, `hangup_unacknowledged_seconds` (null once acknowledged), `hangup_attempt` (which attempt this is; a re-arm increments it) and `already_requested`, which is false for a first or re-armed request and true when an existing one was returned unchanged.

post.description: An explicit Listen action for one selected TTS voice. It accepts a bounded caller sentence (defaulting to a short product sample only when no audio_environment is supplied), keeps no audio or telemetry, and returns a short in-memory WAV only. A selected outgoing audio_environment requires explicit non-blank text and makes a deterministic, headroom-safe local audition; it never substitutes the text, language, voice, or claims a receiver-side final mix. A small per-workspace fixed-window limit protects provider spend. Every language a provider advertises can be previewed. On a platform credential the voice must be one the workspace could browse and select, except an existing saved hosted agent may re-test its exact current platform-managed selection by supplying agent_id when it has disappeared from a listing; arbitrary typed IDs never create shared runtime evidence. With a selected BYOK credential the credential is validated at the provider and then used to render, so any voice id that provider accepts works, and a platform credential is never a fallback. A GPT-Live-1 voice (provider openai, model gpt-live-1) previews differently: it is a short real live session on the platform credential that speaks Skysay's own sample sentence for the requested language, rendered once per voice, language and sample and then served from a tenant-agnostic cache (the response carries text_source: platform_sample and cached). Typed text is refused with error code voice_preview_fixed_sample rather than replaced, credential_id and delivery do not apply, a platform-wide concurrency cap answers 429 when every preview slot is busy, and the preview is never metered as a call.
